<source id="D14:1" doc="D14" title="Agent owners' FAQ" section="Agent owners' FAQ > Can my agent use the biggest model?" date="2026-09-10" type="official">
## Can my agent use the biggest model?

Only on the priority tier. Standard-tier agents can use the smaller and mid-sized models. Moving to priority needs a sign-off from whoever holds your team's budget, and after that you can change the model.
</source>

<source id="D07:0" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Why and by when" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Why and by when

`claude-legacy` was deprecated in v2.5 and will be switched off on 2026-10-31. Any agent still on it that day stops answering. No new agent can be put on it: the registry returns `REG-1010`.
</source>

<source id="D07:4" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 3: Switch" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 3: Switch

Set the new model with `PATCH /agents/{agent_id}`. The change applies from each agent's next session.
</source>

<source id="D03:1" doc="D03" title="Registry changelog" section="Registry changelog > v2.5 — 2026-07-01" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## v2.5 — 2026-07-01

- Deprecated the `claude-legacy` model. Creating an agent with it, or changing an agent to it, now returns `REG-1010`.
- Agents already on `claude-legacy` keep running until 2026-10-31, when the model is switched off. Owners must move them before then; see the model migration runbook.

<source id="D01:9" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Errors

Every error response has the same shape:

```json
{"error": {"code": "REG-1007", "name": "MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED", "message": "claude-opus is not allowed on tier standard"}}
```

The `code` is stable and safe to match on in code; the `message` is for people and may change. The full list is in the error code reference.
</source>

<source id="D14:0" doc="D14" title="Agent owners' FAQ" section="Agent owners' FAQ > My agent suddenly stopped answering. What happened?" date="2026-09-10" type="official">
## My agent suddenly stopped answering. What happened?

Check its status first: someone may have paused it, or it may have hit a spending cap. Then check whether it's on a model that's being switched off. If it's running but every task fails, look at the errors in its logs. An error code starting with `REG-` comes from the registry, and the error code reference explains each one.
</source>

<source id="D02:3" doc="D02" title="Error code reference" section="Error code reference > Monitoring errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Monitoring errors

These come from the monitoring service, not from the Registry API, but they appear in the same alert channels.

| Code | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `MON-2001` | `SCRAPE_FAILED` | Monitoring couldn't collect metrics from one agent. Usually the agent is paused or restarting. |
| `MON-2002` | `REGISTRY_UNREACHABLE` | Monitoring failed to reach the Registry API three times in a row. It raises the `RegistryUnreachable` alert. |
</source>

<source id="prometheus-docs/practices/instrumentation.md:1" doc="prometheus-docs/practices/instrumentation.md" title="Instrumentation" section="Instrumentation > How to instrument" date="2026-09-23" type="vendor">
## How to instrument

The short answer is to instrument everything. Every library, subsystem and
service should have at least a few metrics to give you a rough idea of how it is
performing.

Instrumentation should be an integral part of your code. Instantiate the metric
classes in the same file you use them. This makes going from alert to console to code
easy when you are chasing an error.
</source>

<source id="D02:2" doc="D02" title="Error code reference" section="Error code reference > Limits and availability" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Limits and availability

## Summary

On 2026-08-27, registry-api was unavailable for 42 minutes while registry-db failed over to its standby. Agents that look things up in the registry couldn't finish their tasks, and monitoring lost sight of every agent for the same period.
</source>

<source id="D11:3" doc="D11" title="Incident INC-2093: registry outage during database failover" section="Incident INC-2093: registry outage during database failover > What we changed" date="2026-08-29" type="official">
## What we changed

- An alert now fires when the standby falls more than 60 seconds behind.
- Monitoring keeps its last good agent list when the registry is unreachable, instead of showing nothing.
- `support_agent` now tells users the registry is unavailable instead of failing silently.
</source>

<source id="D11:2" doc="D11" title="Incident INC-2093: registry outage during database failover" section="Incident INC-2093: registry outage during database failover > What made it worse" date="2026-08-29" type="official">
## What made it worse

The failover should have taken about 5 minutes. It took 42 because the standby had fallen 38 minutes behind the primary, and nothing alerted on that lag. For the whole outage, monitoring showed no agents at all, so the on-call engineer couldn't tell which agents were affected. Its agent list comes from the registry.
</source>

<source id="D11:1" doc="D11" title="Incident INC-2093: registry outage during database failover" section="Incident INC-2093: registry outage during database failover > Timeline" date="2026-08-29" type="official">
## Timeline

- 14:10 — The primary registry-db host failed a disk check and failover started.
- 14:11 — `RegistryUnreachable` fired and paged the on-call engineer. The overview dashboard went blank.
- 14:20 — `support_agent` sessions began failing on their first registry lookup. `triage_agent` kept running but couldn't hand tickets over, so 212 tickets queued.
- 14:52 — The standby finished catching up and registry-api recovered. The queued tickets were handed over by 15:05.
</source>

<source id="D09:0" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Summary" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Summary

On 2026-04-08, `billing_agent` failed to issue invoices for 2 hours 15 minutes. Every attempt ended in a timeout from payments-gateway. No customer was charged twice, but 1,140 invoices went out late.
</source>

<source id="D09:3" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > What we changed" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## What we changed

- auth-service now alerts 30 days before any certificate expires.
- payments-gateway now returns an error immediately when a certificate check fails, instead of hanging.
- `billing_agent` stops retrying after three timeouts from the same service in one session.
</source>

<source id="D09:2" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Root cause" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Root cause

payments-gateway checks every request's certificate with auth-service before it will talk to a caller. An intermediate certificate in auth-service expired at 06:00, so every check failed, and payments-gateway timed out instead of returning an error. `billing_agent` treated the timeouts as transient and retried each one until its step limit ran out.
</source>

<source id="D09:1" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Timeline" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Timeline

- 06:02 — `AgentErrorRateHigh` fired for `billing_agent`. No page: it was outside paging hours.
- 08:00 — The on-call engineer saw the alert and found every failed session stuck on the same payments-gateway call.
- 08:40 — The Payments team found that payments-gateway couldn't open connections to auth-service.
- 08:55 — The Identity team renewed the certificate. `billing_agent` recovered within two minutes.
</source>

content.content: ## How requests flow When a request reaches registry-api, it first asks auth-service to validate the `X-Registry-Key` header, then reads or writes registry-db. If auth-service is slow, every registry request is slow; if registry-db is unavailable, registry-api can't answer at all. Monitoring gets its list of agents from registry-api every 30 seconds, then collects metrics from each agent on the list. ## Who to contact Page the owning team through the on-call rota: Platform for registry-api and registry-db, Identity for auth-service, Observability for monitoring, and Search for kb-search. ## Core services - **registry-api** — the Registry API. <source id="D09:2" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Root cause" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Root cause

payments-gateway checks every request's certificate with auth-service before it will talk to a caller. An intermediate certificate in auth-service expired at 06:00, so every check failed, and payments-gateway timed out instead of returning an error. `billing_agent` treated the timeouts as transient and retried each one until its step limit ran out.
</source>

<source id="D09:3" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > What we changed" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## What we changed

- auth-service now alerts 30 days before any certificate expires.
- payments-gateway now returns an error immediately when a certificate check fails, instead of hanging.
- `billing_agent` stops retrying after three timeouts from the same service in one session.
</source>

<source id="D09:1" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Timeline" date="2026-04-10" type="official">

- 06:02 — `AgentErrorRateHigh` fired for `billing_agent`. No page: it was outside paging hours.
- 08:00 — The on-call engineer saw the alert and found every failed session stuck on the same payments-gateway call.
- 08:40 — The Payments team found that payments-gateway couldn't open connections to auth-service.
- 08:55 — The Identity team renewed the certificate. `billing_agent` recovered within two minutes.
</source>

## How requests flow

- **registry-db** — the Postgres database behind registry-api, with a hot standby for failover. Owned by the Platform team.
- **auth-service** — validates registry keys and issues the internal certificates services use to talk to each other. Owned by the Identity team.
- **monitoring** — collects latency and error metrics for every agent and raises alerts. Owned by the Observability team.
- **kb-search** — search over the internal knowledge base, with a response cache in front of it. Owned by the Search team.

## What happened

`research_agent` finds its sources through kb-search. On 2026-06-15 a config change set the kb-search cache's time-to-live to 7 days instead of 7 hours. Every search that had been cached returned the version of each article from when it was first cached, so answers drifted further out of date each day.
</source>

<source id="D10:3" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What we changed" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## What we changed

- kb-search's cache settings are now reviewed like code, and a time-to-live above 24 hours needs the Search team's approval.
- Each kb-search result now carries the date the article was last updated, and `research_agent` includes it when it cites a source.
- Reports produced during the affected week were flagged to their readers.
</source>

<source id="D11:1" doc="D11" title="Incident INC-2093: registry outage during database failover" section="Incident INC-2093: registry outage during database failover > Timeline" date="2026-08-29" type="official">

- 14:52 — The standby finished catching up and registry-api recovered. The queued tickets were handed over by 15:05.

## What happened

`research_agent` finds its sources through kb-search. On 2026-06-15 a config change set the kb-search cache's time-to-live to 7 days instead of 7 hours. Every search that had been cached returned the version of each article from when it was first cached, so answers drifted further out of date each day.

- Reports produced during the affected week were flagged to their readers.
</source>

<source id="D09:2" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Root cause" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Root cause

payments-gateway checks every request's certificate with auth-service before it will talk to a caller. An intermediate certificate in auth-service expired at 06:00, so every check failed, and payments-gateway timed out instead of returning an error. `billing_agent` treated the timeouts as transient and retried each one until its step limit ran out.
</source>

<source id="D04:2" doc="D04" title="Agent platform architecture overview" section="Agent platform architecture overview > How requests flow" date="2026-02-14" type="official">
## How requests flow

When a request reaches registry-api, it first asks auth-service to validate the `X-Registry-Key` header, then reads or writes registry-db. If auth-service is slow, every registry request is slow; if registry-db is unavailable, registry-api can't answer at all.

Monitoring gets its list of agents from registry-api every 30 seconds, then collects metrics from each agent on the list.
</source>

<source id="D09:3" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > What we changed" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## What we changed

- auth-service now alerts 30 days before any certificate expires.
- payments-gateway now returns an error immediately when a certificate check fails, instead of hanging.
- `billing_agent` stops retrying after three timeouts from the same service in one session.
</source>

Each key gets a fixed number of registry calls per minute. If two things share a key, say the agent and a dashboard, they share that allowance. Give the dashboard its own read-only key.

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D08:0" doc="D08" title="Monitoring guide" section="Monitoring guide > What monitoring collects" date="2026-03-02" type="official">
## What monitoring collects

For every agent, monitoring records response time (as p50 and p95), error rate, and the number of sessions. It learns which agents exist by asking the registry for the agent list every 30 seconds, so a new agent appears on the dashboards within a minute of being created.
</source>

<source id="D09:2" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Root cause" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Root cause

payments-gateway checks every request's certificate with auth-service before it will talk to a caller. An intermediate certificate in auth-service expired at 06:00, so every check failed, and payments-gateway timed out instead of returning an error. `billing_agent` treated the timeouts as transient and retried each one until its step limit ran out.
</source>

<source id="D04:2" doc="D04" title="Agent platform architecture overview" section="Agent platform architecture overview > How requests flow" date="2026-02-14" type="official">
## How requests flow

When a request reaches registry-api, it first asks auth-service to validate the `X-Registry-Key` header, then reads or writes registry-db. If auth-service is slow, every registry request is slow; if registry-db is unavailable, registry-api can't answer at all.

Monitoring gets its list of agents from registry-api every 30 seconds, then collects metrics from each agent on the list.
</source>

<source id="D09:3" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > What we changed" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## What we changed

- auth-service now alerts 30 days before any certificate expires.
- payments-gateway now returns an error immediately when a certificate check fails, instead of hanging.
- `billing_agent` stops retrying after three timeouts from the same service in one session.
</source>

<source id="D11:2" doc="D11" title="Incident INC-2093: registry outage during database failover" section="Incident INC-2093: registry outage during database failover > What made it worse" date="2026-08-29" type="official">
## What made it worse

The failover should have taken about 5 minutes. It took 42 because the standby had fallen 38 minutes behind the primary, and nothing alerted on that lag. For the whole outage, monitoring showed no agents at all, so the on-call engineer couldn't tell which agents were affected. Its agent list comes from the registry.
</source>

<source id="D14:3" doc="D14" title="Agent owners' FAQ" section="Agent owners' FAQ > Why does my agent get told to slow down?" date="2026-09-10" type="official">
## Why does my agent get told to slow down?

Each key gets a fixed number of registry calls per minute. If two things share a key, say the agent and a dashboard, they share that allowance. Give the dashboard its own read-only key.
</source>

<source id="D14:2" doc="D14" title="Agent owners' FAQ" section="Agent owners' FAQ > How do I find out which model my agent is on?" date="2026-09-10" type="official">
## How do I find out which model my agent is on?

Look it up in the registry: its record has a `model` field. If you're writing code that runs as the agent, ask the registry "who am I?" with the agent's own key and you'll get the same record back.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D08:0" doc="D08" title="Monitoring guide" section="Monitoring guide > What monitoring collects" date="2026-03-02" type="official">
## What monitoring collects

For every agent, monitoring records response time (as p50 and p95), error rate, and the number of sessions. It learns which agents exist by asking the registry for the agent list every 30 seconds, so a new agent appears on the dashboards within a minute of being created.
</source>

<source id="D04:2" doc="D04" title="Agent platform architecture overview" section="Agent platform architecture overview > How requests flow" date="2026-02-14" type="official">
## How requests flow

When a request reaches registry-api, it first asks auth-service to validate the `X-Registry-Key` header, then reads or writes registry-db. If auth-service is slow, every registry request is slow; if registry-db is unavailable, registry-api can't answer at all.

Monitoring gets its list of agents from registry-api every 30 seconds, then collects metrics from each agent on the list.
</source>

<source id="D04:4" doc="D04" title="Agent platform architecture overview" section="Agent platform architecture overview > Who to contact" date="2026-02-14" type="official">

Page the owning team through the on-call rota: Platform for registry-api and registry-db, Identity for auth-service, Observability for monitoring, and Search for kb-search.
</source>

<source id="D04:1" doc="D04" title="Agent platform architecture overview" section="Agent platform architecture overview > Core services" date="2026-02-14" type="official">
## Core services

- **registry-api** — the Registry API. Stores every agent's configuration. Owned by the Platform team.
- **registry-db** — the Postgres database behind registry-api, with a hot standby for failover. Owned by the Platform team.
- **auth-service** — validates registry keys and issues the internal certificates services use to talk to each other. Owned by the Identity team.
- **monitoring** — collects latency and error metrics for every agent and raises alerts. Owned by the Observability team.
- **kb-search** — search over the internal knowledge base, with a response cache in front of it. Owned by the Search team.
</source>

<source id="D09:2" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Root cause" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Root cause

payments-gateway checks every request's certificate with auth-service before it will talk to a caller. An intermediate certificate in auth-service expired at 06:00, so every check failed, and payments-gateway timed out instead of returning an error. `billing_agent` treated the timeouts as transient and retried each one until its step limit ran out.
</source>

<source id="D09:3" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > What we changed" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## What we changed

- auth-service now alerts 30 days before any certificate expires.
- payments-gateway now returns an error immediately when a certificate check fails, instead of hanging.
- `billing_agent` stops retrying after three timeouts from the same service in one session.
</source>

<source id="D10:1" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What happened" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## What happened

`research_agent` finds its sources through kb-search. On 2026-06-15 a config change set the kb-search cache's time-to-live to 7 days instead of 7 hours. Every search that had been cached returned the version of each article from when it was first cached, so answers drifted further out of date each day.
</source>

<source id="D10:3" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What we changed" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## What we changed

- kb-search's cache settings are now reviewed like code, and a time-to-live above 24 hours needs the Search team's approval.
- Each kb-search result now carries the date the article was last updated, and `research_agent` includes it when it cites a source.
- Reports produced during the affected week were flagged to their readers.
</source>

<source id="D04:1" doc="D04" title="Agent platform architecture overview" section="Agent platform architecture overview > Core services" date="2026-02-14" type="official">
## Core services

- **registry-api** — the Registry API. Stores every agent's configuration. Owned by the Platform team.
- **registry-db** — the Postgres database behind registry-api, with a hot standby for failover. Owned by the Platform team.
- **auth-service** — validates registry keys and issues the internal certificates services use to talk to each other. Owned by the Identity team.
- **monitoring** — collects latency and error metrics for every agent and raises alerts. Owned by the Observability team.
- **kb-search** — search over the internal knowledge base, with a response cache in front of it. Owned by the Search team.
</source>

## Timeline

- 06:02 — `AgentErrorRateHigh` fired for `billing_agent`. No page: it was outside paging hours.
- 08:00 — The on-call engineer saw the alert and found every failed session stuck on the same payments-gateway call.
- 08:40 — The Payments team found that payments-gateway couldn't open connections to auth-service.
- 08:55 — The Identity team renewed the certificate. `billing_agent` recovered within two minutes.
</source>

<source id="D09:0" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Summary" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Summary

On 2026-04-08, `billing_agent` failed to issue invoices for 2 hours 15 minutes. Every attempt ended in a timeout from payments-gateway. No customer was charged twice, but 1,140 invoices went out late.
</source>

<source id="D13:2" doc="D13" title="billing_agent spend limits and approvals" section="billing_agent spend limits and approvals > Why the cap exists" date="2026-09-01" type="official">
## Why the cap exists

In March, a loop bug made `billing_agent` retry failed invoices without a step limit, and it used $2,900 of model calls in one night. The cap limits what any single bug can cost. It isn't a budget target: normal usage is about $2,200 a month.
</source>

<source id="D09:2" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Root cause" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Root cause

payments-gateway checks every request's certificate with auth-service before it will talk to a caller. An intermediate certificate in auth-service expired at 06:00, so every check failed, and payments-gateway timed out instead of returning an error. `billing_agent` treated the timeouts as transient and retried each one until its step limit ran out.
</source>

## Monthly limit

`billing_agent`'s model usage is capped at $4,000 per calendar month. At 80% of the cap, the Finance operations lead gets an email. At 100%, `billing_agent` is set to `paused` until the next month or until the cap is raised.
</source>

<source id="D10:1" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What happened" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## What happened

`research_agent` finds its sources through kb-search. On 2026-06-15 a config change set the kb-search cache's time-to-live to 7 days instead of 7 hours. Every search that had been cached returned the version of each article from when it was first cached, so answers drifted further out of date each day.
</source>

<source id="D10:3" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What we changed" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## What we changed

- kb-search's cache settings are now reviewed like code, and a time-to-live above 24 hours needs the Search team's approval.
- Each kb-search result now carries the date the article was last updated, and `research_agent` includes it when it cites a source.
- Reports produced during the affected week were flagged to their readers.
</source>

<source id="D09:1" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Timeline" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Timeline

- 06:02 — `AgentErrorRateHigh` fired for `billing_agent`. No page: it was outside paging hours.
- 08:00 — The on-call engineer saw the alert and found every failed session stuck on the same payments-gateway call.
- 08:40 — The Payments team found that payments-gateway couldn't open connections to auth-service.
- 08:55 — The Identity team renewed the certificate. `billing_agent` recovered within two minutes.
</source>

<source id="D09:0" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Summary" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Summary

On 2026-04-08, `billing_agent` failed to issue invoices for 2 hours 15 minutes. Every attempt ended in a timeout from payments-gateway. No customer was charged twice, but 1,140 invoices went out late.
</source>

<source id="D13:2" doc="D13" title="billing_agent spend limits and approvals" section="billing_agent spend limits and approvals > Why the cap exists" date="2026-09-01" type="official">
## Why the cap exists

In March, a loop bug made `billing_agent` retry failed invoices without a step limit, and it used $2,900 of model calls in one night. The cap limits what any single bug can cost. It isn't a budget target: normal usage is about $2,200 a month.
</source>

<source id="D09:2" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Root cause" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Root cause

payments-gateway checks every request's certificate with auth-service before it will talk to a caller. An intermediate certificate in auth-service expired at 06:00, so every check failed, and payments-gateway timed out instead of returning an error. `billing_agent` treated the timeouts as transient and retried each one until its step limit ran out.
</source>

<source id="D07:1" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Which agents are affected" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Which agents are affected

As of this writing, two active agents are on `claude-legacy`:

| Agent | Owner | Target model |
|---|---|---|
| `research_agent` | research-team | `claude-sonnet` |
| `notes_agent` | support-team | `claude-haiku` |

Owners can check any agent with `GET /agents/{agent_id}` and look at its `model` field.
</source>

<source id="D04:4" doc="D04" title="Agent platform architecture overview" section="Agent platform architecture overview > Who to contact" date="2026-02-14" type="official">
## Who to contact

Page the owning team through the on-call rota: Platform for registry-api and registry-db, Identity for auth-service, Observability for monitoring, and Search for kb-search.
</source>

</source>

content.content: ## The agents that use them `support_agent` answers customer questions. It looks up agent and account configuration through registry-api and searches help articles through kb-search. `triage_agent` reads incoming tickets and hands the ones it can't close to `support_agent`. ## Who to contact Page the owning team through the on-call rota: Platform for registry-api and registry-db, Identity for auth-service, Observability for monitoring, and Search for kb-search. ## Core services - **registry-api** — the Registry API. Stores every agent's configuration. Owned by the Platform team. - **registry-db** — the Postgres database behind registry-api, with a hot standby for failover. Owned by the Platform team. - **auth-service** — validates registry keys and issues the internal certificates services use to talk to each other. Owned by the Identity team. - **monitoring** — collects latency and error metrics for every agent and raises alerts. Owned by the Observability team. - **kb-search** — search over the internal knowledge base, with a response cache in front of it. Owned by the Search team. ## What happened `research_agent` finds its sources through kb-search. On 2026-06-15 a config change set the kb-search cache's time-to-live to 7 days instead of 7 hours. Every search that had been cached returned the version of each article from when it was first cached, so answers drifted further out of date each day. ## What we changed - kb-search's cache settings are now reviewed like code, and a time-to-live above 24 hours needs the Search team's approval. - Each kb-search result now carries the date the article was last updated, and `research_agent` includes it when it cites a source. - Reports produced during the affected week were flagged to their readers. ## Flags | --storage.agent.path | Base path for metrics storage. Use with agent mode only. | `data-agent/` | | --storage.agent.wal-compression | Compress the agent WAL. If false, the --storage.agent.wal-compression-type flag is ignored. Use with agent mode only. | `true` | | --storage.agent.retention.min-time | Minimum age samples may be before being considered for deletion when the WAL is truncated Use with agent mode only. | `5m` | | --storage.agent.retention.max-time | Maximum age samples may be before being forcibly deleted when the WAL is truncated Use with agent mode only. | `4h` | ## How do I find out which model my agent is on? Look it up in the registry: its record has a `model` field. If you're writing code that runs as the agent, ask the registry "who am I?" with the agent's own key and you'll get the same record back. ## Step 4: Check for rate limiting Look for `REG-1009` responses in the agent's logs. An agent that's being rate-limited waits for `Retry-After` on every call, which looks like latency. If you find them, check whether another process is sharing the agent's key. ## Reading one agent `GET /agents/{agent_id}` returns one agent's full record, or `REG-1005` if no agent has that id. ```json { "agent_id": "research_agent", "model": "claude-legacy", "tier": "standard", "owner": "research-team", "status": "active", "updated_at": "2026-06-23T09:12:44Z" } ``` `GET /agents/me` returns the agent that owns the key making the request. It's the quickest way to check that a newly deployed key works and belongs to the agent you expect. ## What monitoring collects For every agent, monitoring records response time (as p50 and p95), error rate, and the number of sessions. It learns which agents exist by asking the registry for the agent list every 30 seconds, so a new agent appears on the dashboards within a minute of being created.

<source id="D10:1" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What happened" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## What happened

`research_agent` finds its sources through kb-search. On 2026-06-15 a config change set the kb-search cache's time-to-live to 7 days instead of 7 hours. Every search that had been cached returned the version of each article from when it was first cached, so answers drifted further out of date each day.
</source>

<source id="D10:3" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What we changed" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## What we changed

- kb-search's cache settings are now reviewed like code, and a time-to-live above 24 hours needs the Search team's approval.
- Each kb-search result now carries the date the article was last updated, and `research_agent` includes it when it cites a source.
- Reports produced during the affected week were flagged to their readers.
</source>

<source id="D04:4" doc="D04" title="Agent platform architecture overview" section="Agent platform architecture overview > Who to contact" date="2026-02-14" type="official">
## Who to contact

Page the owning team through the on-call rota: Platform for registry-api and registry-db, Identity for auth-service, Observability for monitoring, and Search for kb-search.
</source>

<source id="D04:3" doc="D04" title="Agent platform architecture overview" section="Agent platform architecture overview > The agents that use them" date="2026-02-14" type="official">
## The agents that use them

`support_agent` answers customer questions. It looks up agent and account configuration through registry-api and searches help articles through kb-search. `triage_agent` reads incoming tickets and hands the ones it can't close to `support_agent`.
</source>

<source id="D04:1" doc="D04" title="Agent platform architecture overview" section="Agent platform architecture overview > Core services" date="2026-02-14" type="official">
## Core services

- **registry-api** — the Registry API. Stores every agent's configuration. Owned by the Platform team.
- **registry-db** — the Postgres database behind registry-api, with a hot standby for failover. Owned by the Platform team.
- **auth-service** — validates registry keys and issues the internal certificates services use to talk to each other. Owned by the Identity team.
- **monitoring** — collects latency and error metrics for every agent and raises alerts. Owned by the Observability team.
- **kb-search** — search over the internal knowledge base, with a response cache in front of it. Owned by the Search team.
</source>

## Direct Impacts

   - Monitoring refreshes its agent list from registry-api every 30 seconds
   - Dashboards show no agents during the outage, even though agents may still be running

- Registry API unavailable for **42 minutes**
- **support_agent** sessions began failing on their first registry lookup
- **triage_agent** kept running but couldn't hand over tickets, causing **212 tickets to queue**
- For the entire outage duration, monitoring showed no agents at all

The key issue is that many downstream systems depend on being able to read from the registry, so a registry-db failure creates a cascading outage affecting both operations and business workflows.

Registry-db is a critical dependency that affects:

3. Operational workflows like ticket routing

This pattern was confirmed during Incident INC-2093 in August 2026, where registry-db failed over to its standby for 42 minutes, causing exactly these effects: registry-api downtime, agents unable to complete tasks, and monitoring blind spots [D11:0].

In summary: **registry-api stops working**, which cascades to break **agent operations** and cause **complete monitoring loss**.

<source id="D01:1" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Authentication" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Authentication

Every request must carry a registry key in the `X-Registry-Key` header. A request without one is rejected with `REG-1001`, and a key the registry doesn't recognise is rejected with `REG-1002`.

```bash
curl https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/me \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY"
```

Keys have a scope. A `read` key can call every `GET` endpoint. A `write` key can also create, update and delete agents. Each key belongs to exactly one agent or one person, and the registry records which one made every change. Keys are issued and revoked with `regctl`; see the key rotation runbook.
</source>

<source id="D02:0" doc="D02" title="Error code reference" section="Error code reference > Authentication errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Authentication errors

| Code | Name | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REG-1001` | `MISSING_KEY` | 401 | The request had no `X-Registry-Key` header. |
| `REG-1002` | `INVALID_KEY` | 401 | The key isn't one the registry issued. Check for a truncated or mistyped key. |
| `REG-1003` | `KEY_REVOKED` | 401 | The key was valid but has been revoked. Issue a new key; a revoked key can't be restored. |
| `REG-1004` | `FORBIDDEN_FIELD` | 403 | The key's scope doesn't allow this change. Writes need a `write` key. |
</source>

<source id="D01:1" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Authentication" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Authentication

Every request must carry a registry key in the `X-Registry-Key` header. A request without one is rejected with `REG-1001`, and a key the registry doesn't recognise is rejected with `REG-1002`.

```bash
curl https://registry.internal.example/v2/agents/me \
  -H "X-Registry-Key: $REGISTRY_KEY"
```

Keys have a scope. A `read` key can call every `GET` endpoint. A `write` key can also create, update and delete agents. Each key belongs to exactly one agent or one person, and the registry records which one made every change. Keys are issued and revoked with `regctl`; see the key rotation runbook.
</source>

<source id="D02:0" doc="D02" title="Error code reference" section="Error code reference > Authentication errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Authentication errors

| Code | Name | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REG-1001` | `MISSING_KEY` | 401 | The request had no `X-Registry-Key` header. |
| `REG-1002` | `INVALID_KEY` | 401 | The key isn't one the registry issued. Check for a truncated or mistyped key. |
| `REG-1003` | `KEY_REVOKED` | 401 | The key was valid but has been revoked. Issue a new key; a revoked key can't be restored. |
| `REG-1004` | `FORBIDDEN_FIELD` | 403 | The key's scope doesn't allow this change. Writes need a `write` key. |
</source>

Based on my research across the documentation and database, here are the **recurring causes** across our company incidents:

## Core Patterns Observed Across All 3 Incidents

### 1. **Detection Blind Spots in Monitoring**
All three incidents involved situations where the monitoring system failed to detect the problem until it became apparent through user impact:
- **INC-2041**: `AgentErrorRateHigh` alert fired but was outside paging hours; underlying cert expiration wasn't monitored [D09:1]
- **INC-2067**: No monitoring tracked knowledge freshness; cached results never triggered an alert [D10:0][D10:2]
- **INC-2093**: Registry outage meant monitoring couldn't see *any* agents during the incident - a "monitoring while monitoring" failure [D11:2]

### 2. **Missing Proactive Alerts on Common Failure Modes**
| Incident | Unmonitored Factor | Result |
|----------|-------------------|--------|
| INC-2041 | Certificate expiration in auth-service | No warning; only discovered when billing failed |
| INC-2067 | Knowledge article recency/deadlines | No alert for stale content; user noticed after 7 days |
| INC-2093 | Replica lag during failover | Standby fell 38 min behind; nothing alerted on that gap |

### 3. **Retry Behavior Amplifying Transient Issues**
- **INC-2041**: `billing_agent` retried each payments-gateway timeout until its step limit exhausted, turning what could have been resolved faster into a 2+ hour outage [D09:2]

### 4. **Multi-Touchpoint Cascading Failures**
- INC-2041 touched cross-team dependencies: identity team's auth-service → payments-gateway → billing_agent
- INC-2093 created circular visibility loss: registry down → monitoring blind → engineers unable to assess scope

## Sample Size Caveat

With only 3 historical incidents, statistical significance is limited. However, the **pattern quality** is high - all three incidents share:
- ✗ Missing detection/early warning signals  
- ✗ Cross-team dependency gaps  
- ✓ Clear root causes documented (certs, freshness, replica lag)  
- ✓ Post-mortem remediations implemented  

## Key Insight

The most common failure mode isn't component breakdown — it's **not knowing components will break before it matters**. The incidents show failures occurring in the "grace periods" between expected monitoring events.

Based on my research across the documentation and database, here are the **recurring causes** across our company incidents:

## Core Patterns Observed Across All 3 Incidents

### 1. **Detection Blind Spots in Monitoring**
All three incidents involved situations where the monitoring system failed to detect the problem until it became apparent through user impact:
- **INC-2041**: `AgentErrorRateHigh` alert fired but was outside paging hours; underlying cert expiration wasn't monitored [D09:1]
- **INC-2067**: No monitoring tracked knowledge freshness; cached results never triggered an alert [D10:0][D10:2]
- **INC-2093**: Registry outage meant monitoring couldn't see *any* agents during the incident - a "monitoring while monitoring" failure [D11:2]

### 2. **Missing Proactive Alerts on Common Failure Modes**
| Incident | Unmonitored Factor | Result |
|----------|-------------------|--------|
| INC-2041 | Certificate expiration in auth-service | No warning; only discovered when billing failed |
| INC-2067 | Knowledge article recency/deadlines | No alert for stale content; user noticed after 7 days |
| INC-2093 | Replica lag during failover | Standby fell 38 min behind; nothing alerted on that gap |

### 3. **Retry Behavior Amplifying Transient Issues**
- **INC-2041**: `billing_agent` retried each payments-gateway timeout until its step limit exhausted, turning what could have been resolved faster into a 2+ hour outage [D09:2]

### 4. **Multi-Touchpoint Cascading Failures**
- INC-2041 touched cross-team dependencies: identity team's auth-service → payments-gateway → billing_agent
- INC-2093 created circular visibility loss: registry down → monitoring blind → engineers unable to assess scope

## Sample Size Caveat

With only 3 historical incidents, statistical significance is limited. However, the **pattern quality** is high - all three incidents share:
- ✗ Missing detection/early warning signals  
- ✗ Cross-team dependency gaps  
- ✓ Clear root causes documented (certs, freshness, replica lag)  
- ✓ Post-mortem remediations implemented  

## Key Insight

The most common failure mode isn't component breakdown — it's **not knowing components will break before it matters**. The incidents show failures occurring in the "grace periods" between expected monitoring events.

Page the owning team through the on-call rota: Platform for registry-api and registry-db, Identity for auth-service, Observability for monitoring, and Search for kb-search.

<source id="D15:3" doc="D15" title="Wiki: on-call tips" section="Wiki: on-call tips > Paging etiquette" date="2026-09-20" type="wiki">
## Paging etiquette

When you page another team, say what you've already ruled out. "Registry slow, auth-service latency normal, registry-db CPU at 95%" gets a faster answer than "registry slow, please help."

<source id="D04:2" doc="D04" title="Agent platform architecture overview" section="Agent platform architecture overview > How requests flow" date="2026-02-14" type="official">
## How requests flow

When a request reaches registry-api, it first asks auth-service to validate the `X-Registry-Key` header, then reads or writes registry-db. If auth-service is slow, every registry request is slow; if registry-db is unavailable, registry-api can't answer at all.

Monitoring gets its list of agents from registry-api every 30 seconds, then collects metrics from each agent on the list.
</source>

<source id="D11:1" doc="D11" title="Incident INC-2093: registry outage during database failover" section="Incident INC-2093: registry outage during database failover > Timeline" date="2026-08-29" type="official">

- 14:10 — The primary registry-db host failed a disk check and failover started.
- 14:11 — `RegistryUnreachable` fired and paged the on-call engineer. The overview dashboard went blank.
- 14:20 — `support_agent` sessions began failing on their first registry lookup. `triage_agent` kept running but couldn't hand tickets over, so 212 tickets queued.
- 14:52 — The standby finished catching up and registry-api recovered. The queued tickets were handed over by 15:05.

<source id="D04:1" doc="D04" title="Agent platform architecture overview" section="Agent platform architecture overview > Core services" date="2026-02-14" type="official">
## Core services

- **registry-api** — the Registry API. Stores every agent's configuration. Owned by the Platform team.
- **registry-db** — the Postgres database behind registry-api, with a hot standby for failover. Owned by the Platform team.
- **auth-service** — validates registry keys and issues the internal certificates services use to talk to each other. Owned by the Identity team.
- **monitoring** — collects latency and error metrics for every agent and raises alerts. Owned by the Observability team.
- **kb-search** — search over the internal knowledge base, with a response cache in front of it. Owned by the Search team.
</source>

Based on my research across the documentation and database, here are the **recurring causes** across our company incidents:

## Core Patterns Observed Across All 3 Incidents

### 1. **Detection Blind Spots in Monitoring**
All three incidents involved situations where the monitoring system failed to detect the problem until it became apparent through user impact:
- **INC-2041**: `AgentErrorRateHigh` alert fired but was outside paging hours; underlying cert expiration wasn't monitored [D09:1]
- **INC-2067**: No monitoring tracked knowledge freshness; cached results never triggered an alert [D10:0][D10:2]
- **INC-2093**: Registry outage meant monitoring couldn't see *any* agents during the incident - a "monitoring while monitoring" failure [D11:2]

### 2. **Missing Proactive Alerts on Common Failure Modes**
| Incident | Unmonitored Factor | Result |
|----------|-------------------|--------|
| INC-2041 | Certificate expiration in auth-service | No warning; only discovered when billing failed |
| INC-2067 | Knowledge article recency/deadlines | No alert for stale content; user noticed after 7 days |
| INC-2093 | Replica lag during failover | Standby fell 38 min behind; nothing alerted on that gap |

### 3. **Retry Behavior Amplifying Transient Issues**
- **INC-2041**: `billing_agent` retried each payments-gateway timeout until its step limit exhausted, turning what could have been resolved faster into a 2+ hour outage [D09:2]

### 4. **Multi-Touchpoint Cascading Failures**
- INC-2041 touched cross-team dependencies: identity team's auth-service → payments-gateway → billing_agent
- INC-2093 created circular visibility loss: registry down → monitoring blind → engineers unable to assess scope

## Sample Size Caveat

With only 3 historical incidents, statistical significance is limited. However, the **pattern quality** is high - all three incidents share:
- ✗ Missing detection/early warning signals  
- ✗ Cross-team dependency gaps  
- ✓ Clear root causes documented (certs, freshness, replica lag)  
- ✓ Post-mortem remediations implemented  

## Key Insight

The most common failure mode isn't component breakdown — it's **not knowing components will break before it matters**. The incidents show failures occurring in the "grace periods" between expected monitoring events.

payments-gateway checks every request's certificate with auth-service before it will talk to a caller. ## Summary of Recurring Incident Causes

| Incident | Date | Failed Service | Root Cause |
|----------|------|----------------|------------|
| **INC-2041** | 2026-04-08 | auth-service | Expired intermediate certificate at 06:00; payments-gateway timed out instead of returning errors [D09:2] |

   - **auth-service**: Certificate management issues (infrastructure/cert lifecycle)
   - **kb-search**: Configuration management issues (change approval/review process)
   - **registry-db**: Hardware failures requiring failover infrastructure

2. **Incident Volume**: The database shows only 1 incident per service total (registry-db, kb-search, auth-service).

3. **Root Causes Identified**:
   - auth-service requires proactive alerts before cert expiration (now implemented per INC-2041 postmortem [D09:3])
   - kb-search needs stricter config review process with time limits above 24h requiring approval (now implemented per INC-2067 postmortem [D10:3])
   - registry-db showed no preventative measures documented but uses hot standby failover architecture [D04:1]

Based on my analysis of all incidents in our registry and related documentation, here's what I found about recurring cause patterns:

## Summary of Incidents (Total: 3)

| Incident | Failed Service | Duration | Root Cause |

| INC-2041 | auth-service | 135 min | **Certificate expiration** - intermediate cert expired at 06:00, causing payment gateway timeouts which billing_agent retried until step limit exhausted |
| INC-2067 | kb-search | 10,080 min (~7 days) | **Config drift/TTL misconfiguration** - cache TTL changed from 7h to 7 days, creating 7-day stale caching period |
| INC-2093 | registry-db | 42 min | **Infrastructure failover lag** - primary host disk failure triggered failover, but standby was 38 minutes behind due to no lag monitoring alerts |

## Recurring Cause Patterns Observed

The three incidents reveal three distinct categories of recurring root causes:

### 1. **Infrastructure Monitoring Gaps** (INC-2093)
- No monitoring for service replication lag between primary/standby
- Lack of alerting when infrastructure components fall out of sync
- Result: longer-than-necessary outage windows due to delayed detection

### 2. **Configuration Management Risks** (INC-2067)
- TTL changes affecting cache behavior without proper validation
- Config updates can have cascading effects over extended time periods
- No safeguards against extreme TTL values like 7 days vs 7 hours

### 3. **Service Dependency Failures** (INC-2041)
- Certificate lifecycle management issues causing downstream timeout chains
- Retry mechanisms can exhaust limits even for transient failures
- Interdependent services amplify single points of failure

- All three failed services (**auth-service**, **kb-search**, **registry-db**) each have exactly one incident in the current snapshot

<source id="D09:2" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Root cause" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Root cause

payments-gateway checks every request's certificate with auth-service before it will talk to a caller. An intermediate certificate in auth-service expired at 06:00, so every check failed, and payments-gateway timed out instead of returning an error. `billing_agent` treated the timeouts as transient and retried each one until its step limit ran out.
</source>

<source id="D01:4" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Creating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Creating an agent

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

```json
{"agent_id": "triage_agent", "model": "claude-haiku", "tier": "standard", "owner": "support-team"}
```

Agent ids must be unique: reusing one returns `REG-1006`. The model must be allowed on the agent's tier (see "Tiers and models"), or the request fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D14:1" doc="D14" title="Agent owners' FAQ" section="Agent owners' FAQ > Can my agent use the biggest model?" date="2026-09-10" type="official">
## Can my agent use the biggest model?

Only on the priority tier. Standard-tier agents can use the smaller and mid-sized models. Moving to priority needs a sign-off from whoever holds your team's budget, and after that you can change the model.
</source>

<source id="D07:2" doc="D07" title="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy" section="Runbook: migrating agents off claude-legacy > Step 1: Check the target is allowed" date="2026-07-02" type="official">
## Step 1: Check the target is allowed

Both target models are allowed on the `standard` tier, so neither agent needs a tier change. If you'd rather move to `claude-opus`, the agent must move to the `priority` tier first, or the change fails with `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D03:3" doc="D03" title="Registry changelog" section="Registry changelog > v2.3 — 2026-03-10" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## v2.3 — 2026-03-10

- Added the `tier` field to every agent. Existing agents were set to `standard`.
- Each tier now has an allowlist of models. Assigning a model outside it returns `REG-1007`.
</source>

<source id="D02:1" doc="D02" title="Error code reference" section="Error code reference > Request errors" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Request errors

| Code | Name | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `REG-1005` | `AGENT_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | No agent has this `agent_id`. Ids are case-sensitive. |
| `REG-1006` | `AGENT_NAME_TAKEN` | 409 | An agent with this `agent_id` already exists, including a retired one. |
| `REG-1007` | `MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED` | 422 | The model isn't on the allowlist for the agent's tier. Change the tier first, or pick an allowed model. |
| `REG-1008` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 422 | The body is missing a required field or has a value of the wrong type. The message names the field. |
| `REG-1010` | `MODEL_DEPRECATED` | 422 | The model is deprecated and can't be newly assigned. Currently applies to `claude-legacy`. |
</source>

<source id="D01:5" doc="D01" title="Registry API reference" section="Registry API reference > Updating an agent" date="2026-08-18" type="official">
## Updating an agent

`PATCH /agents/{agent_id}` changes one or more of `model`, `tier`, `owner` and `status`. Send only the fields you're changing. It needs a `write` key; a `read` key gets `REG-1004`.

content.text:
Based on my analysis of all incidents in our registry and related documentation, here's what I found about recurring cause patterns:

## Summary of Incidents (Total: 3)

| Incident | Failed Service | Duration | Root Cause |
|----------|---------------|----------|------------|
| INC-2041 | auth-service | 135 min | **Certificate expiration** - intermediate cert expired at 06:00, causing payment gateway timeouts which billing_agent retried until step limit exhausted |
| INC-2067 | kb-search | 10,080 min (~7 days) | **Config drift/TTL misconfiguration** - cache TTL changed from 7h to 7 days, creating 7-day stale caching period |
| INC-2093 | registry-db | 42 min | **Infrastructure failover lag** - primary host disk failure triggered failover, but standby was 38 minutes behind due to no lag monitoring alerts |

## Recurring Cause Patterns Observed

The three incidents reveal three distinct categories of recurring root causes:

### 1. **Infrastructure Monitoring Gaps** (INC-2093)
- No monitoring for service replication lag between primary/standby
- Lack of alerting when infrastructure components fall out of sync
- Result: longer-than-necessary outage windows due to delayed detection

### 2. **Configuration Management Risks** (INC-2067)
- TTL changes affecting cache behavior without proper validation
- Config updates can have cascading effects over extended time periods
- No safeguards against extreme TTL values like 7 days vs 7 hours

### 3. **Service Dependency Failures** (INC-2041)
- Certificate lifecycle management issues causing downstream timeout chains
- Retry mechanisms can exhaust limits even for transient failures
- Interdependent services amplify single points of failure

## Key Observations

- All three failed services (**auth-service**, **kb-search**, **registry-db**) each have exactly one incident in the current snapshot
- The registry contains agents running models across different tiers: `claude-opus` (priority), `claude-haiku`, and `claude-sonnet` (standard)
- Only limited longitudinal data is available in the incident log (just 3 total incidents)

Would you like me to search for more specific operational patterns or investigate particular teams that own these services?

<source id="D10:1" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What happened" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## What happened

`research_agent` finds its sources through kb-search. On 2026-06-15 a config change set the kb-search cache's time-to-live to 7 days instead of 7 hours. Every search that had been cached returned the version of each article from when it was first cached, so answers drifted further out of date each day.
</source>

<source id="D10:3" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What we changed" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## What we changed

- kb-search's cache settings are now reviewed like code, and a time-to-live above 24 hours needs the Search team's approval.
- Each kb-search result now carries the date the article was last updated, and `research_agent` includes it when it cites a source.
- Reports produced during the affected week were flagged to their readers.
</source>

<source id="D10:0" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > Summary" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## Summary

From 2026-06-15 to 2026-06-22, `research_agent` answered questions with knowledge-base articles that had since been updated. Nothing failed and no alert fired; a user noticed that a report quoted a policy that had changed four days earlier.
</source>

<source id="D10:2" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > Why it took a week to notice" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## Why it took a week to notice

The agent's latency and error rate looked better than usual: cached answers are fast and never fail. Nothing in monitoring measures whether results are current. The only signal was a person comparing an answer with the source.

`POST /agents` creates an agent. It needs a `write` key. The body must include `agent_id`, `model`, `tier` and `owner`; `status` defaults to `active`.

| `REG-1005` | `AGENT_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | No agent has this `agent_id`. Ids are case-sensitive. |
| `REG-1006` | `AGENT_NAME_TAKEN` | 409 | An agent with this `agent_id` already exists, including a retired one. |
| `REG-1007` | `MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED` | 422 | The model isn't on the allowlist for the agent's tier. Change the tier first, or pick an allowed model. |
| `REG-1008` | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 422 | The body is missing a required field or has a value of the wrong type. The message names the field. |

Based on my analysis of all incidents in our registry and related documentation, here's what I found about recurring cause patterns:

## Summary of Incidents (Total: 3)

| Incident | Failed Service | Duration | Root Cause |
|----------|---------------|----------|------------|
| INC-2041 | auth-service | 135 min | **Certificate expiration** - intermediate cert expired at 06:00, causing payment gateway timeouts which billing_agent retried until step limit exhausted |
| INC-2067 | kb-search | 10,080 min (~7 days) | **Config drift/TTL misconfiguration** - cache TTL changed from 7h to 7 days, creating 7-day stale caching period |
| INC-2093 | registry-db | 42 min | **Infrastructure failover lag** - primary host disk failure triggered failover, but standby was 38 minutes behind due to no lag monitoring alerts |

## Recurring Cause Patterns Observed

The three incidents reveal three distinct categories of recurring root causes:

### 1. **Infrastructure Monitoring Gaps** (INC-2093)
- No monitoring for service replication lag between primary/standby
- Lack of alerting when infrastructure components fall out of sync
- Result: longer-than-necessary outage windows due to delayed detection

### 2. **Configuration Management Risks** (INC-2067)
- TTL changes affecting cache behavior without proper validation
- Config updates can have cascading effects over extended time periods
- No safeguards against extreme TTL values like 7 days vs 7 hours

### 3. **Service Dependency Failures** (INC-2041)
- Certificate lifecycle management issues causing downstream timeout chains
- Retry mechanisms can exhaust limits even for transient failures
- Interdependent services amplify single points of failure

## Key Observations

- All three failed services (**auth-service**, **kb-search**, **registry-db**) each have exactly one incident in the current snapshot
- The registry contains agents running models across different tiers: `claude-opus` (priority), `claude-haiku`, and `claude-sonnet` (standard)
- Only limited longitudinal data is available in the incident log (just 3 total incidents)

<source id="D09:3" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > What we changed" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## What we changed

- auth-service now alerts 30 days before any certificate expires.
- payments-gateway now returns an error immediately when a certificate check fails, instead of hanging.
- `billing_agent` stops retrying after three timeouts from the same service in one session.
</source>

<source id="D09:2" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Root cause" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Root cause

payments-gateway checks every request's certificate with auth-service before it will talk to a caller. An intermediate certificate in auth-service expired at 06:00, so every check failed, and payments-gateway timed out instead of returning an error. `billing_agent` treated the timeouts as transient and retried each one until its step limit ran out.
</source>

<source id="D09:1" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Timeline" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Timeline

- 06:02 — `AgentErrorRateHigh` fired for `billing_agent`. No page: it was outside paging hours.
- 08:00 — The on-call engineer saw the alert and found every failed session stuck on the same payments-gateway call.
- 08:40 — The Payments team found that payments-gateway couldn't open connections to auth-service.
- 08:55 — The Identity team renewed the certificate. `billing_agent` recovered within two minutes.
</source>

<source id="prometheus-docs/introduction/overview.md:8" doc="prometheus-docs/introduction/overview.md" title="Overview" section="Overview > When does it not fit?" date="2026-09-23" type="vendor">
## When does it not fit?

Prometheus values reliability. You can always view what statistics are
available about your system, even under failure conditions. If you need 100%
accuracy, such as for per-request billing, Prometheus is not a good choice, as
the collected data will likely not be detailed and complete enough. In such a
case, you would be best off using some other system to collect and analyze the
data for billing, and Prometheus for the rest of your monitoring.
</source>

## What happened

`research_agent` finds its sources through kb-search. On 2026-06-15 a config change set the kb-search cache's time-to-live to 7 days instead of 7 hours. Every search that had been cached returned the version of each article from when it was first cached, so answers drifted further out of date each day.

<source id="D10:3" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What we changed" date="2026-06-24" type="official">

- kb-search's cache settings are now reviewed like code, and a time-to-live above 24 hours needs the Search team's approval.
- Each kb-search result now carries the date the article was last updated, and `research_agent` includes it when it cites a source.
- Reports produced during the affected week were flagged to their readers.
</source>

- **registry-api** — the Registry API. Stores every agent's configuration. Owned by the Platform team.
- **registry-db** — the Postgres database behind registry-api, with a hot standby for failover. Owned by the Platform team.
- **auth-service** — validates registry keys and issues the internal certificates services use to talk to each other. Owned by the Identity team.
- **monitoring** — collects latency and error metrics for every agent and raises alerts. Owned by the Observability team.
- **kb-search** — search over the internal knowledge base, with a response cache in front of it. Owned by the Search team.

The failover should have taken about 5 minutes. It took 42 because the standby had fallen 38 minutes behind the primary, and nothing alerted on that lag. ## Timeline

- 14:10 — The primary registry-db host failed a disk check and failover started.
- 14:11 — `RegistryUnreachable` fired and paged the on-call engineer. The overview dashboard went blank.
- 14:20 — `support_agent` sessions began failing on their first registry lookup. `triage_agent` kept running but couldn't hand tickets over, so 212 tickets queued.
- 14:52 — The standby finished catching up and registry-api recovered. The queued tickets were handed over by 15:05.
</source>

<source id="postgresql/high-availability.md:5" doc="postgresql/high-availability.md" title="High Availability, Load Balancing, and Replication" section="High Availability, Load Balancing, and Replication > Comparison of Different Solutions" date="2026-09-28" type="vendor">
## Comparison of Different Solutions

Shared Disk Failover  
Shared disk failover avoids synchronization overhead by having only one copy of the database. It uses a single disk array that is shared by multiple servers. If the main database server fails, the standby server is able to mount and start the database as though it were recovering from a database crash. This allows rapid failover with no data loss.
</source>

<source id="prometheus-docs/introduction/overview.md:8" doc="prometheus-docs/introduction/overview.md" title="Overview" section="Overview > When does it not fit?" date="2026-09-23" type="vendor">
## When does it not fit?

Prometheus values reliability. You can always view what statistics are
available about your system, even under failure conditions. If you need 100%
accuracy, such as for per-request billing, Prometheus is not a good choice, as
the collected data will likely not be detailed and complete enough. In such a
case, you would be best off using some other system to collect and analyze the
data for billing, and Prometheus for the rest of your monitoring.
</source>

## What happened

`research_agent` finds its sources through kb-search. On 2026-06-15 a config change set the kb-search cache's time-to-live to 7 days instead of 7 hours. Every search that had been cached returned the version of each article from when it was first cached, so answers drifted further out of date each day.

<source id="D10:3" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What we changed" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## What we changed

- kb-search's cache settings are now reviewed like code, and a time-to-live above 24 hours needs the Search team's approval.
- Each kb-search result now carries the date the article was last updated, and `research_agent` includes it when it cites a source.
- Reports produced during the affected week were flagged to their readers.
</source>

<source id="D04:1" doc="D04" title="Agent platform architecture overview" section="Agent platform architecture overview > Core services" date="2026-02-14" type="official">

- **auth-service** — validates registry keys and issues the internal certificates services use to talk to each other. Owned by the Identity team.
- **monitoring** — collects latency and error metrics for every agent and raises alerts. Owned by the Observability team.
- **kb-search** — search over the internal knowledge base, with a response cache in front of it. Owned by the Search team.

<source id="D09:2" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Root cause" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Root cause

payments-gateway checks every request's certificate with auth-service before it will talk to a caller. An intermediate certificate in auth-service expired at 06:00, so every check failed, and payments-gateway timed out instead of returning an error. `billing_agent` treated the timeouts as transient and retried each one until its step limit ran out.
</source>

<source id="D09:3" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > What we changed" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## What we changed

- auth-service now alerts 30 days before any certificate expires.
- payments-gateway now returns an error immediately when a certificate check fails, instead of hanging.
- `billing_agent` stops retrying after three timeouts from the same service in one session.
</source>

<source id="D09:1" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Timeline" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Timeline

- 06:02 — `AgentErrorRateHigh` fired for `billing_agent`. No page: it was outside paging hours.
- 08:00 — The on-call engineer saw the alert and found every failed session stuck on the same payments-gateway call.
- 08:40 — The Payments team found that payments-gateway couldn't open connections to auth-service.
- 08:55 — The Identity team renewed the certificate. `billing_agent` recovered within two minutes.
</source>

<source id="D09:0" doc="D09" title="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices" section="Incident INC-2041: billing_agent unable to issue invoices > Summary" date="2026-04-10" type="official">
## Summary

On 2026-04-08, `billing_agent` failed to issue invoices for 2 hours 15 minutes. Every attempt ended in a timeout from payments-gateway. No customer was charged twice, but 1,140 invoices went out late.
</source>

<source id="D13:0" doc="D13" title="billing_agent spend limits and approvals" section="billing_agent spend limits and approvals > Monthly limit" date="2026-09-01" type="official">

`billing_agent`'s model usage is capped at $4,000 per calendar month. At 80% of the cap, the Finance operations lead gets an email. At 100%, `billing_agent` is set to `paused` until the next month or until the cap is raised.

<source id="postgresql/high-availability.md:5" doc="postgresql/high-availability.md" title="High Availability, Load Balancing, and Replication" section="High Availability, Load Balancing, and Replication > Comparison of Different Solutions" date="2026-09-28" type="vendor">
## Comparison of Different Solutions

Shared Disk Failover  
Shared disk failover avoids synchronization overhead by having only one copy of the database. It uses a single disk array that is shared by multiple servers. If the main database server fails, the standby server is able to mount and start the database as though it were recovering from a database crash. This allows rapid failover with no data loss.
</source>

- **auth-service** — validates registry keys and issues the internal certificates services use to talk to each other. Owned by the Identity team.
- **monitoring** — collects latency and error metrics for every agent and raises alerts. Owned by the Observability team.
- **kb-search** — search over the internal knowledge base, with a response cache in front of it. Owned by the Search team.

<source id="D10:1" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What happened" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## What happened

`research_agent` finds its sources through kb-search. On 2026-06-15 a config change set the kb-search cache's time-to-live to 7 days instead of 7 hours. Every search that had been cached returned the version of each article from when it was first cached, so answers drifted further out of date each day.
</source>

<source id="D10:3" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > What we changed" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## What we changed

- kb-search's cache settings are now reviewed like code, and a time-to-live above 24 hours needs the Search team's approval.
- Each kb-search result now carries the date the article was last updated, and `research_agent` includes it when it cites a source.
- Reports produced during the affected week were flagged to their readers.
</source>

<source id="D10:0" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > Summary" date="2026-06-24" type="official">

From 2026-06-15 to 2026-06-22, `research_agent` answered questions with knowledge-base articles that had since been updated. Nothing failed and no alert fired; a user noticed that a report quoted a policy that had changed four days earlier.

<source id="D10:2" doc="D10" title="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results" section="Incident INC-2067: research_agent returning outdated results > Why it took a week to notice" date="2026-06-24" type="official">
## Why it took a week to notice

The agent's latency and error rate looked better than usual: cached answers are fast and never fail. Nothing in monitoring measures whether results are current. The only signal was a person comparing an answer with the source.
</source>

Page the owning team through the on-call rota: Platform for registry-api and registry-db, Identity for auth-service, Observability for monitoring, and Search for kb-search.
</source>

## Asynchronous Commit

If the database crashes during the risk window between an asynchronous commit and the writing of the transaction's WAL records, then changes made during that transaction *will* be lost. The duration of the risk window is limited because a background process (the “WAL writer”) flushes unwritten WAL records to disk every section guc-wal-writer-delay milliseconds. The actual maximum duration of the risk window is three times `wal_writer_delay` because the WAL writer is designed to favor writing whole pages at a time during busy periods.

> [!CAUTION]
> An immediate-mode shutdown is equivalent to a server crash, and will therefore cause loss of any unflushed asynchronous commits.

<source id="postgresql/wal.md:1" doc="postgresql/wal.md" title="Reliability and the Write-Ahead Log" section="Reliability and the Write-Ahead Log > Reliability" date="2026-09-28" type="vendor">
## Reliability

Reliability is an important property of any serious database system, and PostgreSQL does everything possible to guarantee reliable operation. One aspect of reliable operation is that all data recorded by a committed transaction should be stored in a nonvolatile area that is safe from power loss, operating system failure, and hardware failure (except failure of the nonvolatile area itself, of course). Successfully writing the data to the computer's permanent storage (disk drive or equivalent) ordinarily meets this requirement. In fact, even if a computer is fatally damaged, if the disk drives survive they can be moved to another computer with similar hardware and all committed transactions will remain intact.
</source>
